correctness.rationale: The measurement counts all starts including wraparound and repeated windows. Rotation/reversal preserve it; complementation is not factored out. Complementary windows pair weight a at length k with R−a at length n−k, where R is total weight. My exhaustive replay marked rotations and reversals from each first unvisited binary string and grouped the resulting bracelets by separately sorted full-length window-weight lists, computed by prefix sums on the doubled word. Through n=11 there was no collision. At n=12 there were 224 bracelets and 223 observations, with sole nonsingleton class {001011001101, 001011010011}. Separately grouping by the complete ordered-lag two-point vector reproduced all 23 pairs in the CSV and the (length, count) breakdown (0,1),(3,17),(4,3),(5,2). Expansion of each squared window sum gives F_k=kR+2Σ_{d=1}^{k−1}(k−d)C_d, so second differences recover each C_d; there is no converse. A window of length 12q+s in either r-fold power adds 6q to the corresponding remainder weight and each base start occurs r times. A dihedral equivalence of the powers would restrict on twelve consecutive letters to one between the bases. This proves repetition for all r, not other lengths. Replay: python3 /workspace/review-replay.py 3 with the original homometric_pairs_n12.csv path as its argument.
